terms.grammar: conjunction, with the subjunctive in the tense the main verb calls for; without a verb, “as it were”
evidence: Ter. Eun. 3.2.8: assimulābō, quasi nunc exeam (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fin. 5.43: in puerīs virtūtum quasi scintillās vidēmus
Traupman 106: he left under the pretext that …, hinc abiit quasi (+ subj.)
terms.comment: “As if” with a clause: the verb is subjunctive, present or perfect after a present main verb (not the imperfect of English “as if he were”). Without a verb it softens a word used loosely: quasi scintillās, “sparks, as it were”.

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the subjunctive; without a verb, “like”
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.42: parvī enim prīmō ortū sīc jacent, tamquam omnīnō sine animō sint
Cic. Att. 8.14.2: ego tēcum tamquam mēcum loquor

terms.grammar: conjunction, with the subjunctive; without a verb, “like”
evidence: Liv. 1.56.12: velut sī prōlāpsus cecidisset, terram ōsculō contigit
Liv. 5.41.9: ad eōs velut simulācra versī
terms.comment: Livy’s favourite; velutī is the fuller form.
